title: Verticalized Ecosystem Recon: Model Availability & Risk Dossier
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Produce a compact, evidence-backed dossier that maps model availability, latency economics, and substitution risk across three target verticals (FinServ EU, SMB search, Healthcare US). Scope: three-week rapid recon combining (1) telemetry sampling from production workloads, (2) third-party model cataloging and license constraints, and (3) buyer/prospect interviews. Outcome: prioritized list of 8 high-risk supply gaps, a supply-fragility index per vertical, recommended short-term fallback bundles (hosted + quantized fallbacks), and an experiment plan to validate fallback UX and econometrics. Deliverables: 1) Confluence dossier with signals and recommended mitigations; 2) lightweight dashboard with regional availability heatmap; 3) a 2-week field test plan to run fallback rollouts for 2 paying customers. Timeline: research spike (week 1), telemetry ingest + mapping (week 2), synthesis + field-plan (week 3).

2025-01-29 | Arjun Patel: Ingest ETL PoC completed. Preliminary heatmap shows two open-source models with 40% regional availability in EU cloud providers under our latency SLO. Created GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/recon/PR-342.
2025-02-05 | Design review (Sasha Ivanov): Requested inclusion of a simplified fallback decision flow for customer-facing docs. Action: add 'fallback experience' wireframe to dossier by Feb 10.

2025-02-20 | Product review (Leah Martinez): Prioritization rubric approved (impact x probability). Top high-risk items: regional breakage for quantized variants and license blocking for two academic-licensed models in production bundles.
2025-02-28 | Arjun Patel: Draft dossier ready for PM review. Dashboard prototype link included below. Next: align with Solutions Eng for two pilot customers and finalize field test checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence dossier includes per-vertical supply-fragility index and top 8 prioritized supply gaps with evidence links
Dashboard prototype shows regional availability and 99p latency overlays for >8 model variants
Two pilot customers consent to a controlled 2-week fallback roll-out plan and measurable KPIs (latency, error rate, cost delta)
Hand-off ticket to Solutions Eng + Customer Success with clear runbook and rollback criteria
notes: Trade-offs: choosing broader telemetry sampling increases signal quality but risks delaying deliverables; compromise is to sample heavier for top-3 customer regions and lightweight sampling for others.
Engineering feedback: kernel-level quant variants are inconsistently labeled across model sources; normalization layer required (see GH issue #349).
Regulatory note: EU FinServ vertical requires license provenance checks - legal has flagged two models with non-commercial academic clauses; recommend reserve capacity for alternative variants.
Design feedback: customers prefer explicit UX choices (auto-fallback vs. manual opt-in) — field tests should parameterize both options.
Next steps: finalize dossier and schedule cross-functional review 2025-03-03; prepare two Solutions Eng runbooks for pilot onboarding by 2025-03-10.
